ruleName: Ball Lost or Out of Bounds: Stroke-and-Distance Relief Must Be Taken
title: Are White Stakes Themselves Out of Bounds?
question: White stakes define out of bounds. Is the stake itself in bounds?

choices.text: No, the stake itself is out of bounds.
Only if a Local Rule says so.
Only if the committee marks it as such.

explanation: The boundary edge of the course is defined by the course-side points of the white stakes at ground level. The stakes themselves are out of bounds.

juniorVersion.title: Are White Out of Bounds Posts Out of Bounds Too?
juniorVersion.question: When you see white posts that show 'out of bounds,' is the post itself out of bounds?

choices.text: No, the post is out of bounds.
Only if a special rule says so.
Only if people running the game say so.

juniorVersion.explanation: White posts that show where 'out of bounds' starts are not part of the course. The post itself is out of bounds.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A place you are not allowed to play from. It is usually shown with white posts.
A stick or marker in the ground. Here, it means a white one that shows 'out of bounds'.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show kids a real out of bounds post and explain you can't play from that spot or touch it when dropping a ball.
likelyMisconceptions: Some kids may think the post is still on the course because it touches the ground.
Some may think you can lean on it or touch it for a drop.
